epic.title: Admin Surface (CLI + UI + API)
epic.description: Build the complete admin surface for the MTC CA: an axum admin API defined by OpenAPI (spec §17.2), the mtcctl CLI built with clap v4 (§17.3), and an htmx+Askama+SSE web UI embedded in the CA service binary (§17.4) — with enforced full CLI/UI parity so every operation is available on both surfaces (§17.1). Both consumers ride the foundation-owned OpenAPI codegen pipeline, and each admin operation lands vertically: OpenAPI change, server handler, CLI subcommand, UI view, and CLI-driven E2E test (§17.5, §19.13).

tickets.title: Admin API core: axum crate serving OpenAPI-generated server stubs
tickets.description:
## Goal
Stand up `crates/admin` as the admin API core (spec §17.2): an axum app mounting routes from OpenAPI-generated Rust server stubs. This is the single API both mtcctl and the UI consume, and the anchor for all admin-surface work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin` exists with `lib.rs` mounting API routes (axum), per the layout in §17.4
- Routes implemented against Rust server stubs generated from `api/admin.openapi.yaml` via `make api-gen` (foundation pipeline)
- Health/version endpoint implemented end-to-end as the first operation (spec -> stub -> handler)
- Shared JSON error model (problem-details style) with typed handler errors
- `AppState` seam injects CA-service state handles as trait objects so handlers run against the memory backend in tests
- API mounted in the CA service binary, reachable on localhost:8080 in dev mode

## Out of Scope
- IAM auth middleware (adm-auth-middleware)
- UI routes/templates (adm-ui-shell)
- Business operations beyond health/version (per-operation tickets)
- The codegen pipeline itself (foundation-infra: openapi-codegen-pipeline)

## Testing
- Unit: handler tests against in-memory AppState (§19.1, no external deps)
- Integration: axum/tower test client over the mounted router; check that regenerated code compiles in CI

## Demo
`cargo run -p ca-service` (dev mode) then `curl localhost:8080/api/healthz` returns JSON status.

tickets.title: mtcctl CLI skeleton: clap v4 tree, generated client wiring, output formats
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/mtcctl` with the full clap v4 (derive) subcommand tree from §17.3, wired to the OpenAPI-generated Rust client, with the global output-format contract agents and scripts rely on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/mtcctl` binary with the complete §17.3 subcommand tree declared; unimplemented leaves exit non-zero with a clear 'not yet implemented' message
- Global flags: `--output human|json|yaml` (human default), `--endpoint`, `--yes`/`--confirm` plumbed through (enforcement in adm-privileged-confirm)
- Uses the OpenAPI-generated Rust client (§17.2) for all API calls; no hand-rolled HTTP
- Output layer: human tables, `--output json` and `--output yaml` via serde on the same response types
- `mtcctl status` returns live data from the health/version endpoint as first working command
- Errors map to distinct exit codes; stderr for diagnostics, stdout for payload

## Out of Scope
- Individual operation implementations (per-operation tickets)
- REPL and shell completion (adm-repl, adm-completion)
- Request signing (adm-auth-middleware)

## Testing
- Unit: clap parse tests (`Command::debug_assert`), output-format snapshot tests
- Integration: run binary against an in-process axum test server; assert JSON output is stable

## Demo
`mtcctl status --output json | jq .version` against `make demo` environment.

tickets.title: Admin UI shell: htmx + Askama layout, rust-embed static assets
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the basic admin UI shell (roadmap Phase 0; spec §17.4): Askama compile-time templates, vendored htmx, static assets embedded via rust-embed, served from the same axum app as the API.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin/templates/` with `layout.html`, `partials/`, `pages/` structure per §17.4; `templates.rs` holds Askama template structs
- `static/` with vendored `htmx.min.js` and `styles.css`, embedded via `rust-embed` and served from the binary (no external CDN, no JS build toolchain)
- UI routes mounted in `crates/admin` `lib.rs` alongside API routes
- Dashboard placeholder page renders with nav linking every planned view from the §17.4 table (stub pages OK)
- Askama compile-time checking active: a template referencing a missing field fails the build

## Out of Scope
- SSE real-time updates (adm-sse-stream)
- Real data on any page (per-operation tickets)
- Tree visualization (observability epic)

## Testing
- Unit: template render tests for layout and placeholder pages
- Integration: axum test client asserts 200 + text/html for each route and embedded asset

## Demo
`make demo` then open `localhost:8080` — dashboard shell with nav renders, assets load offline.

tickets.title: mtcctl shell completion (bash, zsh, fish)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl completion` per §17.3 so operators and agents get shell completion for the full subcommand tree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl completion bash|zsh|fish` emits a valid completion script via `clap_complete` derived from the real command tree
- Completion output goes to stdout so it can be sourced or installed (`mtcctl completion bash > ...`)
- Unsupported shell arguments produce a clear error listing supported shells
- README/CLI help documents installation per shell

## Out of Scope
- Dynamic completion of server-side values (batch IDs, indices)
- REPL tab-completion (adm-repl)

## Testing
- Unit: generation succeeds for all three shells; snapshot test that bash output contains top-level subcommands
- E2E: shell script sources the bash completion under bash and asserts no syntax error

## Demo
`source <(mtcctl completion bash)` then tab-complete `mtcctl lo<TAB>` to `log`.

tickets.title: Admin API auth: SigV4 verification middleware + CLI request signing
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement authentication for the admin surface per §17.3: AWS IAM via signed requests on the API, with mtcctl signing requests from the standard AWS credential chain, plus a dev-mode bypass so everything still runs on a laptop (§1 non-goals, §18).

## Acceptance Criteria
- tower middleware on `crates/admin` API routes verifies SigV4 signatures; unauthenticated requests get 401 with the shared error model
- Privileged operations are tagged in `api/admin.openapi.yaml` (e.g. `x-privileged: true`) and the middleware enforces an elevated principal for them (403 otherwise)
- mtcctl signs requests using the AWS default credential chain; works against LocalStack-style dummy credentials
- Dev bypass requires BOTH a `dev-auth` cargo feature and `MTC_DEV_AUTH=off` config; a test asserts a build without the feature returns 401 regardless of the config flag
- htmx UI form posts hit the same middleware-protected API routes; dev bypass covers them in `make demo`; non-dev browser auth is documented as out of scope for v1 (laptop-only, §1)

## Out of Scope
- CLI confirmation prompts (adm-privileged-confirm)
- Real IAM policy authoring / CDK roles (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: signature verification accept/reject, privileged-tag enforcement, dev bypass gating
- Integration: mtcctl against test server with dummy creds; tampered signature rejected

## Demo
`mtcctl status` succeeds with dummy AWS creds; `curl` without signature gets 401 (dev bypass off).

tickets.title: Privileged-command confirmation flow (--confirm / --yes)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the §17.3 authorization UX: privileged mtcctl commands require explicit `--confirm` or an interactive confirmation prompt, skippable with `--yes` for automation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shared helper in `crates/mtcctl` that privileged subcommands call before issuing the API request
- Behavior: `--confirm` proceeds; interactive TTY prompts y/N; non-TTY without `--confirm`/`--yes` fails with a clear error and non-zero exit
- `--yes` skips prompting (automation path) and is logged to stderr
- Prompt text names the operation and its target (e.g. 'initiate failover to us-west-2')
- Helper adopted by any already-merged privileged command; documented convention for future ones

## Out of Scope
- Server-side privilege enforcement (adm-auth-middleware)
- Specific privileged operations themselves (their own tickets)

## Testing
- Unit: TTY/non-TTY matrix, flag combinations, exit codes
- E2E: shell script asserts a privileged stub refuses without `--yes` and proceeds with it

## Demo
`mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` prompts; `--yes` proceeds non-interactively.

tickets.title: SSE stream: real-time state push into the UI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the Server-Sent Events stream (§17.4): CA service state changes (new batches, lease events, audit results) push into the UI without polling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin/src/handlers/sse.rs` exposes an SSE endpoint on the admin app (axum `Sse` responder)
- Typed event enum (batch-sealed, lease-changed, audit-completed, checkpoint-signed) serialized as named SSE events with JSON data
- Bridged from the CA service's in-process notification channel via the AppState seam; slow consumers are dropped/lagged without blocking the service (broadcast semantics)
- Layout wires the htmx SSE extension so subscribed partials refresh on matching events; browser reconnect works (retry + Last-Event-ID tolerated)
- Heartbeat/keepalive comments prevent idle proxy timeouts

## Out of Scope
- Producing the events inside the CA service (ca-service epic)
- Per-page partials consuming specific events (per-operation tickets)

## Testing
- Unit: event serialization, broadcast lag/drop behavior
- Integration: test client subscribes, injects events via AppState, asserts stream frames; disconnect/reconnect test

## Demo
`make demo`, open dashboard, watch batch tiles update live as the sample ACME client issues certs — no page refresh.
deps: EXTERNAL:CA service in-process event notifications for state changes (batches, lease, audit)

tickets.title: Status + log inspect: mtcctl status, log inspect, live dashboard
tickets.description:
## Goal
Ship the Phase 3 'Admin API + CLI + UI for status/inspection' slice: `mtcctl status` (service status, lease, checkpoint) and `mtcctl log inspect` (log size, recent batches), plus a dashboard showing overall health, current state, and growth rate (§17.3, §17.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations for status and log-state added to `api/admin.openapi.yaml`; `make api-gen` regenerates cleanly (§17.5 flow)
- Server handlers read live CA state: role, latest checkpoint (age, tree size), recent batch summaries; the lease block renders a 'single-region' placeholder value until lease-epoch-protocol lands (adm-lease-ops replaces it)
- `mtcctl status` and `mtcctl log inspect` render human tables and stable `--output json|yaml`
- Dashboard page shows the same fields (parity) plus growth rate computed as entries/hour over the last N batches; auto-refresh via `hx-trigger` polling, with SSE swap-over tracked in adm-sse-stream
- CLI help text and UI tooltips document each field (§17.5 step 7)

## Out of Scope
- Batch drill-down (adm-batch-ops)
- Proof operations (adm-proof-ops)
- Failover readiness (adm-failover-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against memory backend with seeded state
- Integration: LocalStack-backed service, CLI asserts real values
- E2E: `tests/e2e/status.sh` drives mtcctl per §19.13

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl status` and `mtcctl log inspect`; dashboard shows matching numbers.

tickets.title: Batch operations: mtcctl batch list/inspect + Batches UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl batch list` and `mtcctl batch inspect` plus the Batches UI view with status and drill-down (§17.3, §17.4 key views).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: list recent batches (paginated, newest first) and get batch by ID with full details (entry count, tree range, checkpoint ref, timestamps, status)
- Handlers read via the storage facade; work against memory backend and LocalStack
- `mtcctl batch list` human table + `--output json`; `mtcctl batch inspect <id>` shows full details; unknown ID exits non-zero with a clean error
- Batches UI page lists batches with status and links to a drill-down partial (hx-get); list auto-updates on batch-sealed SSE events when the stream exists
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented (§17.5)

## Out of Scope
- Tree visualization of batch contents (observability epic)
- Per-cert lookup (adm-cert-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers with seeded memory-backend batches; pagination edges (empty log, single batch)
- Integration: against LocalStack-backed facade
- E2E: `tests/e2e/batch-list.sh` — issue certs, assert new batch appears via CLI

## Demo
`make demo`, wait one batch cadence, `mtcctl batch list` then `mtcctl batch inspect <id>`; same drill-down in UI.

tickets.title: Cert operations: mtcctl cert issue/lookup + Cert lookup UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl cert issue` (test issuance via the ACME adapter) and `mtcctl cert lookup` (per-cert info by index or PEM), plus the Cert lookup UI view (§17.3, §17.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: trigger test issuance for a domain; lookup cert by index or uploaded PEM returning TBSCert contents, batch ref, checkpoint, and current status
- `mtcctl cert issue --domain X` outputs the issued cert (PEM to stdout); `mtcctl cert lookup --index N` / `--pem FILE` renders details, `--output json` stable for scripting (§19.13 example)
- Cert lookup UI page: form (index or PEM paste) rendering the same fields (parity)
- Nonexistent index returns 404 -> non-zero CLI exit with clean message
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Full forensics fields — served-proof audit trail, pruning status (§20.2; observability epic extends this endpoint)
- `cert revoke` (adm-revocation-ops)
- The ACME endpoint itself (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers with memory backend; PEM parse failure paths
- Integration: issue-then-lookup against LocalStack demo stack
- E2E: `tests/e2e/issuance-and-verification.sh` per §19.13

## Demo
`mtcctl cert issue --domain test.example.com > /tmp/cert.pem && mtcctl cert lookup --pem /tmp/cert.pem`.
deps: EXTERNAL:ACME endpoint adapter for test issuance (ca-service epic)

tickets.title: mtcctl repl: interactive command shell
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl repl` (§17.3, §18.6): an interactive, agent-friendly command shell that reuses the existing clap tree — deterministic, scriptable, output captured.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl repl` starts a line-oriented shell; each line is parsed with the same clap definitions as one-shot invocation (no divergent grammar)
- Works with piped stdin for scripting (reads until EOF, exits 0); errors on a line are reported but do not kill the session in interactive mode
- Session-scoped settings persist (`--output json` set once applies to subsequent commands)
- `help`, `exit`/EOF, and command history (interactive TTY only) supported
- `--output` behavior identical to one-shot mode so captured output is stable

## Out of Scope
- The evcxr Rust REPL / `make repl` (local-dev-experience epic)
- Tab-completion of server-side values

## Testing
- Unit: line parsing reuses clap tree; error-continues semantics
- E2E: pipe a script of commands into `mtcctl repl` against the demo stack, assert outputs

## Demo
`echo -e 'status\nbatch list' | mtcctl repl` prints both results in order.

tickets.title: Automated CLI/UI parity check over the OpenAPI spec
tickets.description:
## Goal
Enforce §17.1 full parity mechanically: a CI-run test walks every operation in `api/admin.openapi.yaml` and fails if it lacks a CLI subcommand or a UI surface mapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Convention: each OpenAPI operation carries `x-cli-command` and `x-ui-view` extensions (or an explicit `x-parity-exempt` with justification)
- Test parses the spec, asserts every `x-cli-command` resolves to a real path in the mtcctl clap tree, and every `x-ui-view` resolves to a registered UI route/template
- Missing or dangling mappings fail `cargo test` with an actionable message naming the operation
- Existing operations annotated; check wired into the standard test run (CI required check via existing pipeline)
- Convention documented for future operation tickets

## Out of Scope
- Runtime behavioral equivalence between CLI and UI (covered by per-operation E2E)
- CI infrastructure itself (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: the parity test itself, plus negative fixtures (spec with missing annotation fails)

## Demo
Delete an `x-cli-command` line locally, run `cargo test -p admin parity`, watch it fail with the operation named.

tickets.title: Dev-mode fake clock control endpoint on the admin API
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose the dev-mode fake clock over the admin API (§18.4): the CA service's injected `Clock` is controllable so `make time-advance` (owned by local-dev-experience) has something to call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations (dev-only tag): get current simulated time; advance by duration (e.g. `days=400`)
- Handler drives the injected fake `Clock` through the AppState seam; returns new simulated time
- Compiled/enabled only in dev mode — in non-dev config the routes are absent (404), verified by test
- `mtcctl` dev subcommand (e.g. `mtcctl dev time-advance --days N`) wired for scriptability, marked dev/test only in help
- Advancing time emits a log line with old/new time for auditability

## Out of Scope
- The `Clock` trait and fake-clock implementation (ca-service epic)
- `make time-advance` wrapper target (local-dev-experience epic)

## Testing
- Unit: advance math, dev-gating (routes absent outside dev)
- Integration: advance clock against demo stack, assert service-observed time moved

## Demo
`mtcctl dev time-advance --days 400 && mtcctl status` shows checkpoint timestamps jumped forward.
deps: EXTERNAL:injected Clock interface with dev fake clock (ca-service epic)

tickets.title: Docs: adding a new admin operation end-to-end
tickets.description:
## Goal
Document the §17.5 workflow so any contributor or agent can add an admin operation: update OpenAPI -> `make api-gen` -> server handler -> clap subcommand -> htmx UI -> E2E test -> help text/tooltips.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/adding-an-admin-operation.md` walks the seven §17.5 steps using the status/log-inspect operation as the worked example, with real file paths (`api/admin.openapi.yaml`, `crates/admin/src/handlers/`, `crates/mtcctl/`, `crates/admin/templates/`, `tests/e2e/`)
- Documents the parity annotations (`x-cli-command`, `x-ui-view`) and privileged-op tagging conventions
- Documents output-format and exit-code conventions for new subcommands, and the CLI-help/UI-tooltip requirement
- Linked from the repo README/AGENTS context so agents discover it

## Out of Scope
- General agent harness docs (agent-harnessing epic)
- Operation-specific runbooks (observability epic)

## Testing
- Doc-only PR; CI verifies referenced paths exist (simple link/path check script if available)

## Demo
Follow the doc to add a trivial echo operation on a branch; both `mtcctl` and the UI gain it and the parity check passes.

tickets.title: Proof operations: mtcctl log inclusion/consistency/verify + UI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Ship the Phase 4 'CLI commands for proof inspection and verification' (§17.3): `mtcctl log inclusion`, `log consistency`, and `log verify`, with a matching UI form for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: inclusion proof for an index, consistency proof between two sizes, verify-cert-against-log; handlers delegate to read-path proof generation and the verification library
- `mtcctl log inclusion --index N` prints the proof and local verification result; `--output json` includes `verified: true|false` (§19.13 example shape)
- `mtcctl log consistency --from A --to B` generates and verifies; invalid ranges (A>B, B>tree size) fail cleanly with non-zero exit
- `mtcctl log verify --pem FILE` verifies a certificate end-to-end against the log
- UI page/partial for proof queries showing verification outcome (parity); CLI help + tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Proof generation internals and the verification library (read-path epic)
- Self-auditor consistency sweeps (adm-audit-ops / observability)

## Testing
- Unit: handler validation edges against memory backend
- Integration: proofs against LocalStack demo log
- E2E: extend `tests/e2e/issuance-and-verification.sh` — issue, then verify inclusion via CLI

## Demo
`mtcctl cert issue --domain d.test > c.pem && mtcctl log verify --pem c.pem --output json | jq .verified` prints true.
deps: EXTERNAL:verification library + inclusion/consistency proof generation (read-path epic)

tickets.title: Lease operations: mtcctl lease show/renew + Lease UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose lease state over the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4): `mtcctl lease show` (current holder, expiry) and `mtcctl lease renew` (force renewal, dev/test only), plus the Lease UI view with history and force-renew.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: get lease state (holder region, epoch, acquired/expiry times, recent transitions) and force-renew (tagged dev/test-only, absent or 403 outside dev mode)
- Handlers read from the lease/epoch protocol implementation; no lease logic duplicated in the admin layer
- `mtcctl lease show` human + `--output json`; `mtcctl lease renew` clearly marked dev/test in help and refuses outside dev mode
- Lease UI page: current holder, expiry countdown, transition history, force-renew button (dev mode); updates on lease-changed SSE events
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Lease/epoch protocol internals and Kani harnesses (multi-region epic)
- Failover commands (adm-failover-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against memory-backend lease state; dev-gating of renew
- Integration: `make demo-multiregion` stack — show reflects real holder; renew extends expiry
- E2E: shell script asserts holder/epoch fields present via CLI

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion` then `mtcctl lease show`; watch expiry move after `mtcctl lease renew`.

tickets.title: Failover exposure: mtcctl failover status/initiate + UI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose manual failover on the admin surface (§13.2, §17.3): `mtcctl failover status` (readiness assessment) and `mtcctl failover initiate` (privileged), plus UI equivalents. Orchestration internals belong to multi-region; this ticket is the API/CLI/UI exposure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: failover readiness (replication lag, standby health, prerequisites) and initiate (privileged; requires `--to <region>` and `--reason`, per §13.2 justification + incident ref)
- Handlers delegate to the multi-region failover orchestrator; admin layer holds no promotion logic
- `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2 --reason "..."` goes through the confirmation flow (adm-privileged-confirm) and streams/echoes step progress from the idempotent promotion procedure (§13.3)
- Initiate tagged `x-privileged`; request without elevated principal gets 403 (adm-auth-middleware enforcement, covered by test)
- `mtcctl failover status --output json` stable for runbook automation
- Failover UI panel: readiness display + initiate form with confirmation (parity with §13.2 'CLI or admin UI')

## Out of Scope
- Promotion procedure, readiness computation, standby mode (multi-region epic)
- Automated failover (non-goal, §1)

## Testing
- Unit: handler delegation, privileged gating, required-args validation
- Integration: `make demo-multiregion` — initiate against simulated partition
- E2E: chaos-style shell script partitioning a region then failing over via CLI (§18.3)

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion && make partition-region us-east-1 && mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2 --reason drill --yes`.
deps: EXTERNAL:manual failover orchestration + readiness assessment (multi-region epic)

tickets.title: Audit operations: mtcctl audit run/history/verify + Audit UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose the self-auditor on the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4): `mtcctl audit run` (on-demand trigger), `audit history`, and `audit verify` (independent log-consistency verification), plus the Audit UI view. Self-auditor exposure is part of the cosigner-free trust story (§25.8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: trigger audit run, list audit history (result, timestamp, checked range), run independent consistency verification
- Handlers delegate to the self-auditor service; admin layer performs no auditing itself
- `mtcctl audit run` returns run ID and outcome (or polls to completion with `--wait`); `audit history --output json` stable; `audit verify` exits non-zero on inconsistency (usable in scripts/CI)
- Audit UI page: history table with pass/fail badges, manual-run button; updates on audit-completed SSE events
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Self-auditor Lambda/implementation and scheduling (observability epic)
- Compliance reports (adm-report-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed auditor in memory backend
- Integration: demo stack — trigger run, see result in history
- E2E: `tests/e2e/audit.sh` runs audit via CLI and asserts pass

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl audit run --wait && mtcctl audit history`; same in the Audit page.
deps: EXTERNAL:self-auditor service with on-demand trigger + history store (observability epic)

tickets.title: Report operations: mtcctl report issuance/revocation/compliance + Reports UI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose report generation on the admin surface (§17.3, §20.3: reports signed by a separate reporting key, generated via `mtcctl report`): issuance log report, revocation report, and compliance bundle, plus the Reports UI view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: generate issuance, revocation, and compliance reports with time-range parameters; responses include the report artifact (or a storage ref) and its signature
- `mtcctl report issuance|revocation|compliance --from --to` writes the report to stdout or `--out FILE`; `--output json` wraps with metadata (range, signature, generated-at)
- JSON output includes the detached signature (base64) and reporting key ID; E2E asserts both fields are non-empty
- Reports UI page: form to request each report type and download the result (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Report content assembly and reporting-key signing internals (observability epic)
- Audit runs (adm-audit-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handler parameter validation, empty-range behavior
- Integration: generate reports against demo stack with issued+revoked certs
- E2E: shell script generates compliance bundle and asserts signature + key ID fields present

## Demo
`mtcctl report compliance --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-07-01 --out bundle.tar.gz` then download the same from the Reports page.

tickets.title: Prune operations: mtcctl prune status/run + UI panel
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose pruning on the admin surface (§17.3, §15): `mtcctl prune status` (watermark and pending work) and `mtcctl prune run` (trigger workflow), plus a UI panel for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: pruning status (watermark, eligible ranges, last run) and trigger-run; handlers are thin proxies to the pruning workflow interface
- `mtcctl prune status --output json` stable; `mtcctl prune run` returns an execution ID and non-zero exit on rejected trigger
- UI panel on an appropriate page shows watermark + pending work with a run button
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Pruning Step Functions workflow and retention enforcement (pruning epic)
- Revocation commands (adm-revocation-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed pruning interface (memory backend)
- Integration: trigger against LocalStack demo, watermark advances
- E2E: `tests/e2e/prune.sh` — load fixture, run prune via CLI, assert watermark moved

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=million-entries && mtcctl prune run && mtcctl prune status`.

tickets.title: Revocation operations: mtcctl revocation list/add/distribute, cert revoke + UI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose revocation on the admin surface (§17.3, §16): `mtcctl revocation list`, `revocation add` (privileged), `revocation distribute` (emergency redistribution), and `mtcctl cert revoke` (privileged single-cert path), plus UI for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: get current revocation list, add range (privileged), trigger emergency distribution, revoke single cert by index (privileged)
- Handlers delegate to the revocation service; privileged ops tagged `x-privileged` and enforced server-side (403 without elevated principal, via adm-auth-middleware)
- `mtcctl revocation add --range A-B` and `mtcctl cert revoke --index N` require the confirmation flow; `revocation list --output json` stable
- `mtcctl revocation distribute` triggers the §16.3 emergency flow and reports distribution outcome
- Revocation UI: list view with add-range and distribute actions behind confirmation (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Revocation Lambda, list format, distribution mechanisms (revocation epic)
- Revocation report (adm-report-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handler validation (bad ranges, overlaps), privileged gating
- Integration: revoke-then-list against demo stack
- E2E: `tests/e2e/revocation.sh` — issue, revoke via CLI, `cert lookup` shows revoked (§19.1 demo scenario)

## Demo
`mtcctl cert revoke --index 5 --yes && mtcctl revocation list` shows the entry; UI matches.

tickets.title: Adapter operations: mtcctl adapter list/status/pause + Adapters UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose intake adapters on the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4, §10): `mtcctl adapter list`, `adapter status` (per-adapter health and intake rate), and `adapter pause` (privileged), plus the Adapters UI view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: list configured adapters, per-adapter status (health, intake rate, last entry), pause/resume (privileged)
- Handlers read from the adapter health/observability surface behind the EntryIntake seam; works with only the ACME adapter configured (v1 reality, §25.9)
- `mtcctl adapter status --output json` stable; `adapter pause <name>` requires confirmation flow and reflects paused state in subsequent status
- Pause/resume tagged `x-privileged` and enforced server-side (403 without elevated principal, via adm-auth-middleware)
- Adapters UI page: per-adapter health/intake tiles with pause/resume controls (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Adapter SDK, AWS Private CA adapter, health-surface internals (adapter-pattern epic)
- EntryIntake trait itself (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed adapter registry (memory backend); pause state machine edges
- Integration: pause ACME adapter in demo stack, assert intake stops
- E2E: shell script pauses/resumes via CLI and asserts status transitions

## Demo
`mtcctl adapter pause acme --yes && mtcctl adapter status` shows paused; sample issuance loop stalls, then resume.
